articles.headline: Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to 'public benefit fund'
keyFacts: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic announced it will commit 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund.
Anthropic stated the fund could support nonprofit organisations and address AI impacts on the jobs market.
The announcement comes as Anthropic prepares for a potential stock market listing.
body: - Published
Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to a fund that will make donations for the "public good".
The announcement comes as Anthropic lays the ground for a potential blockbuster stock market listing that could value the firm at more than $1tn (Â£750bn).

The AI industry has come under intense scrutiny recently over safety concerns and fears about its impact on society and the economy. Anthropic reportedly said in its initial public offering (IPO) filing that AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity".
Anthropic said its proposed fund could support nonprofit organisations, and efforts to address AI's impact on the jobs market.
None of the shares held by the the fund would be used for lobbying or political donations in the US or overseas, it added.
Anthropic's Public Benefit Fund could also receive another 2% of the firm's shares at its board's discretion, the Claude developer said in a statement released on Sunday.
Technology billionaire Elon Musk responded to the announcement on social media with: "I recommend giving the shares directly to the public." "This is what I will be doing," he added.
Last week, Anthropic told prospective investors that its revenue surged by 45% to $16.8bn (Â£12.6bn) in the three months to the end of September.

In common with other AI firms, it is seeking to position itself as being able to generate huge profits despite spending billions on developing the technology and building infrastructure to power its models.
Companies around the world, primarily technology firms, have cut thousands of jobs after investing in AI, with many pointing to higher efficiencies from its adoption.

Research by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) published in 2024 suggested that almost 40% of jobs around the world will be affected by AI, with that figure rising as high as â60% in advanced economies.
In September, a researcher who quit Anthropic said people working on the technology were "genuinely frightened" about the speed of its advancements and what it could mean for humanity.
"I believe that if we don't slow down at the current rate of progress, there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future," he said.
Jacob Coxon was speaking to the BBC after his resignation post on the dangers of AI went viral on a backdrop of growing safety concerns about the industry.
The 27-year-old's former boss, Anthropic head Dario Amodei, had previously called for AI development to slow down - though some have questioned the motivations behind this.

The bosses of two rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Musk, have both said they agree with Amodei's proposal for industry-wide deceleration and regulation, as well as independent monitoring of AI model development.
Earlier this month, US President Donald Trump and the heads of major AI firms signed a "morally binding" document, making them responsible for ensuring the safety of their own technology.
Trump has repeatedly rejected the idea of laws to control development of the technology despite a debate about the potential risks of AI and what it means for humanity.

Since then, the president has named the director of national intelligence Jay Clayton as the head of a new taskforce on AI which, he said, will co-ordinate government engagement with consumers, companies and "religious organizations".

articles.headline: France's government under pressure after weekend of widespread violence
keyFacts: Around 1,500 businesses were looted and about 1,000 police officers were injured during protests across France, the interior ministry said.
President Emmanuel Macron faced criticism from political rivals and unions for his response to the unrest.
Prime Minister Lecornu called a crisis cabinet meeting Monday, while groups announced further mass protests for 5 November.
body: - Published

France's Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu is holding a crisis cabinet meeting on Monday to assess a weekend of violence and looting across the country, in what were some of the worst scenes of public disorder in modern French history.

On Saturday over half a million mainly peaceful protesters demonstrated against rising living costs and dwindling access to decent public services, including a good state education. But the protests turned nasty after groups of black-clad, masked activists and vandals appeared.

An estimated 1,500 shops and businesses were looted and destroyed. Riot police fired tear gas and turned water cannon on crowds. They were seen hitting people with batons in several places. France's interior ministry said about 1,000 police officers were injured on Saturday, seven of them seriously.

There had been rumours in France that President Emmanuel Macron may introduce a temporary curfew in parts of the country, or even impose a state of emergency to help calm the febrile atmosphere. In the end, he used a televised address to the nation on Sunday to call for national unity and to try to assure the French public that the perpetrators of the violence would be punished.
Macron's speech has been roundly criticised on social media forums and by political opponents for lacking concrete detail.
How will vandals and rioters now be brought to account?
How might France's towns and cities be better protected - especially since new mass demonstrations have been announced in a couple of weeks' time?
Exactly how will destroyed businesses be compensated?
And when will a dialogue be established with students and teachers' bodies on the subject of education?

On Sunday the Secretary General of the CGT union, Sophie Binet, accused Macron of failing to address students' concerns, the cost-of-living crisis or the dwindling quality of public services in France.

He's apparently passed that baton to Prime Minister Lecornu. Yet he and his interior minister are charged by many in France with being woefully ill-prepared and under-policed ahead of Saturday's multiple, scheduled protests.
The president of France's lower house of parliament, YaÃ«l Braun-Pivet, says she wants to open an inquiry into exactly what happened this weekend and why.
"Things are dark in the city of light [a nickname for Paris]" was the graffiti I read daubed in red paint across a wall adjacent to a row of shattered shops in the French capital on Sunday night.

Macron is widely viewed here as a lame-duck president. He is on his way out. There's a hotly contested race under way to become his successor, with the vote scheduled in six months' time. The presidential candidate from the anti-immigration nationalist right (Marine Le Pen) and also the anti-capitalist left (Jean-Luc Melenchon) are vying to make headlines.
That is adding to current tensions in France - in politics as well as on the streets.
Parliament here is paralysed, deeply divided between three vying political blocks.

Then there are France's financial woes too. Investors are leaning hard on this country to get its spiralling public debt under control. But the French government worries, if it cuts public services or welfare, yet more angry people will pour out onto the streets.
What now, what next, is our country broken? You hear these questions a lot at the moment.
People across France were shocked and troubled by Saturday's events. The images of tear-gassed towns, apparently unimpeded looters and burning public buildings have worried the nation.

Many passers-by I speak to express frustration that, while they worry about the future, their leading politicians seem, instead, to be passionately focused on finger-pointing; blaming one another for the volatility.
"While we worry for our safety, they use this situation as a pre-presidential election political football," teacher and father of three Edouard told me.

Macron and his prime minister blamed Saturday's violent chaos on radical far left groups and delinquents; hard left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon alleged government "incompetence"; Marine Le Pen on the nationalist right, which likes to be seen as strong on law and order, posted a video seated in front of the French flag, giving a presidential-style address blaming the "Macronist administration that is out of steam, exhausted, and disoriented".
For the next two weeks, the French authorities hope for a bit of a respite. Students start their half-term break as of Monday.

But on 5 November, a cross-section of trade unions, plus France's disparate "yellow jacket" (gilets jaunes) movement that staged demonstrations for over a year in 2018 - during Macron's first term as president - have announced huge protests.
France is holding its breath.

articles.headline: Anthropic says it will commit small percentage of stock to ‘public benefit’ fund
keyFacts: Anthropic announced plans to commit five percent of its stock to a new Public Benefit Fund.
The company said the fund aims to alleviate concerns that AI could cause instability for many workers.
Anthropic is widely expected to go public later this year, according to Reuters.
body: One of the country’s largest artificial intelligence companies, Anthropic , said on Sunday it plans to disburse a small percentage of its stock to a “Public Benefit Fund.”
In a blog post titled, ”Investing in the public benefit,” the AI lab outlines a “new entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows.”

The company cites a need for “bolder approaches” to alleviating concerns AI could “cause instability for many workers.” Anthropic’s announcement comes after a summer and early fall in which data center construction and cybersecurity and safety worries emerged as key themes surrounding AI policy. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei penned a significant thought-leadership essay in mid-September calling for stronger guardrails on the pace of the technology’s development, and polling shows the public holds an overtly negative view of the industry.

“Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline,” the announcement also says.

Conversations surrounding Universal Basic Income have long run alongside debates about AI and other emerging technologies’ existential societal impact, and Sunday’s announcement signals an early movement toward redistributing AI wealth in some manner.

The post referenced Anthropic’s status as a public benefit corporation, a structure that requires management to balance turning a profit for investors with achieving a stated public mission. The company says its activities “have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company,” and Anthropic is widely expected to go public later this year, according to Reuters . The entity will also have the flexibility to “explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.”
FUTURE OF PENTAGON’S AI AND AUTONOMY PUSH IS IN LIMBO WITHOUT RECONCILIATION: ‘PLENTY OF BLAME TO GO AROUND’

Elon Musk, who heads Grok, Tesla, and SpaceX, expressed support for the idea on social media on Sunday night, saying, “I recommend giving the shares directly to the public,” before saying, “This is what I will be doing.”

AI has become an increasingly important topic impacting November’s midterm elections . Lawmakers nationwide have had to grapple with the public’s shifting perception of the technology’s impact and the industry’s reputation. The fund will function as a “wholly-owned LLC,” rather than a traditional nonprofit, according to the company, and will not be used for lobbying or political donations.

articles.headline: The Best 'Peanuts' Great Pumpkin Comic Strip Came Out 2 Years Before the Famous TV Special
keyFacts: The Great Pumpkin was first mentioned in a Peanuts comic strip on October 26, 1959, two years before the television special debuted in 1966.
Charles Schulz published multiple strips featuring Linus writing letters, waiting in pumpkin patches, and trying to convince others of the Great Pumpkin.
In October 1964, a multi-week storyline about Linus running for class president ended when he ruined his election chances by talking about the Great Pumpkin.
body: In 1966, CBS debuted the now-classic television special, It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown. In it, all the kids in the Peanuts gang take part in typical Halloween activities, including trick-or-treating and pumpkin-carving — except for Linus. Instead, Linus is preparing for the arrival of a mythical being known as the “Great Pumpkin.”

As Linus explains, “Each year, the Great Pumpkin rises out of the pumpkin patch that he thinks is the most sincere,” then he distributes toys to the children waiting for him. Linus spends the special writing letters to the Great Pumpkin and trying to convince others of its existence. Then he spends Halloween night in a pumpkin patch, awaiting the Great Pumpkin’s arrival. Of course, the Great Pumpkin never emerges, but Linus still vows to wait again next year.
To the casual Peanuts fan, that may be all they ever know of Linus and the Great Pumpkin, but dedicated readers of the Peanuts comic strip know there’s much, much more to the story.

The Great Pumpkin was first mentioned in a Peanuts comic on Oct. 26, 1959. In it, Linus is writing a letter to the Great Pumpkin when Lucy asks, “What in the world are you doing?” In reply, Linus says, “Don’t you know? This is the time of year when we all write to the ‘Great Pumpkin’ and tell him what we want for Halloween. The ‘Great Pumpkin’ loves little children. I can see him now, rising up out of the pumpkin patch with his big bag of toys!” Meanwhile, Lucy just stares at him, dumbfounded.
The very next day, Charles Schulz released a similar strip with Linus again chattering on about the Great Pumpkin, while Charlie Brown stares blankly at him.
There are a few more strips where people just stare at Linus in disbelief. Charlie Brown eventually tells him, “You’re crazy.”
Of course, the Great Pumpkin never arises out of the earth to disperse presents. And it certainly doesn’t respond to any letters. Charlie Brown and Lucy even tease Linus about it after Halloween.

For the next few years, Schulz would repeat the pattern. During the last week of October, he’d have Linus write more letters to the Great Pumpkin and preach about the Great Pumpkin’s impending arrival. In 1960, he convinces Charlie Brown to wait in the pumpkin patch with him, and Charlie Brown asks a very good question. “It just occurred to me that there must be ten million pumpkin patches in this country… What makes you think we’re in the right one?”

Then 1961 featured a couple of particularly funny Great Pumpkin comic strips. In this one, Linus cites the recent historical record for Great Pumpkin appearances. “On Halloween night in 1959, the Great Pumpkin appeared in the pumpkin patch of Boots Rutman in Connecticut,” says Linus. He also says, “In 1960, the Great Pumpkin appeared in the pumpkin patch of R.W. Daniels of Texas.” The specificity here is very, very funny, so much so that it surprises me that this wasn’t also used in the TV special, as many of the Great Pumpkin strips predating the special made their way into that script.

Then there’s this one, which is basically the Peanuts equivalent of that Tiger King meme where Joe Exotic says, “I am never gonna financially recover from this.” In the strip, Linus explains to Lucy that he has to believe in the Great Pumpkin, and that he’s already sent out 57 pumpkin cards. Then Linus says, “It would be economically disastrous for me not to believe it!”

I was surprised to find that Linus successfully converts Lucy to Great Pumpkinism in 1962. Lucy even starts her own pumpkin patch in an effort to lure the Great Pumpkin and get a whole bunch of presents. However, Linus tells her that her pumpkin patch is completely hypocritical — most likely because of her greed — which prompts her to give up and just sell her pumpkins instead.

If you go back through the October Peanuts archives and read a bunch of Great Pumpkin comic strips back-to-back, the effect is twofold. For one, for those who have watched the TV special a bunch but haven’t read these strips before, it feels like you’re getting deleted scenes from the special, and it's a lot of fun to see the other ways Linus tries to convince his friends of the Great Pumpkin’s existence and all the different ways they find him to be ridiculous.

The other effect of reading a lot of these strips at once is that Linus feels a bit different. In the special, he seems like he simply has a quirky belief, but the strips make Linus look like he’s an obsessed madman. It makes everything related to the Great Pumpkin that much funnier. This feeling pays off particularly well if you go back and read the entire month of Peanuts comics from October 1964.

Generally, Schulz would do Great Pumpkin-themed strips just a few days before Halloween — maybe one week before, at most — then he would usually take the first day or two of November to show Linus complaining that he’d missed the Great Pumpkin again. But in 1964, he did things a bit differently. On Oct. 5, 1964, Schulz began a multi-week storyline about Linus running for class president. 1964 was an election year, and this was just a month away from the presidential election, so it was a timely storyline for Schulz.

For two weeks straight, pretty much everything in the comic strip was all about Linus’ run for office, and Linus is a very good candidate. He makes powerful, even somewhat revolutionary speeches, which get his classmates all riled up. He keeps on rising in the polls. Linus is all set to win the election, then on Oct. 21, Schulz — and Linus — did something completely unexpected. While making his rousing final speech before the election, Linus talks about the Great Pumpkin, which immediately destroys his run for office.

If the strip is taken on its own, the context is still clear about Linus running for office and how one extreme political position or misstep in a single speech can destroy a candidate’s chances. But the fact that Schulz spent two whole weeks ignoring the Great Pumpkin only to then make it the entire focus in the end is beyond brilliant. It also makes Linus seem downright deranged for his beliefs. The time and patience this took illustrates Schulz’s sheer brilliance as both a storyteller and a joke-teller, which is why it takes the cake — or, maybe, pumpkin pie? — as the greatest Great Pumpkin strip ever.

articles.headline: Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv makes emergency landing after bomb threat
keyFacts: An Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna made an emergency landing in Sofia after receiving a bomb threat, Bulgarian authorities said.
A Bulgarian MiG-29 fighter jet escorted the Airbus A320 carrying 51 passengers and six crew members after a general emergency signal was transmitted.
Austrian Airlines stated that passengers will be rebooked on alternative flights as quickly as possible once a security search of the plane is complete.
body: An Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna made an emergency landing in Sofia on Sunday after a bomb threat, Bulgarian authorities said.
The Airbus A320 landed safely with 51 passengers and six crew members aboard after reportedly receiving a bomb threat near the Bulgarian-Romanian border.
"During the flight, on the border with Romania, the crew reported a bomb threat signal and decided to land in Sofia extraordinarily," the Bulgarian transport ministry said in a statement.
Fighter jet escorts plane
The Airbus A320 plane was flying from Tel Aviv for Vienna but was diverted to Sofia in Bulgaria at 9:25 p.m., air tracker Flightradar24 data showed.
Data from another flight-tracking platform, ADS-B Exchange, showed that the flight transmitted a squawk code 7700, a signal for a general emergency, around the time it was diverted.
A Bulgarian MiG-29 fighter jet was scrambled to escort the aircraft.
Following the evacuation of passengers after landing, a security search of the plane was launched, Austrian Airlines said in a statement quoted by Austrian news agency APA.
"Once the search of the aircraft is complete, the passengers will be rebooked onto alternative flights as quickly as possible," the airline said.
Last month, the co-pilot of Flydubai flight was suspected of attacking his pilot in the cockpit, and attempting to hijack the plane and crash it intentionally in Israel.

articles.headline: Steam Week in Review: Steam Next Fest has over 8,000 demos, as worthless vibe coded slop levels up
keyFacts: Steam Next Fest features over 8,000 demos on its press preview landing page, roughly double the amount from June 2026.
Alliance Arts Inc. canceled its public demo for Drunken Goddess Reflux over concerns that AI tools would enable rapid cloning.

body: We are drowning in shit. Steam Next Fest, which kicks off tomorrow, currently has 8,011 matches on its press preview landing page. That's roughly double the amount of demos featured in Steam's June 2026 Next Fest. In June 2022, Next Fest boasted just over a thousand demos.
The vast majority of these demos will be meritless slop. And I daresay many of them—though I have no way to confirm—didn't exist as concepts before October.

If you use social media, especially X, you've probably noticed an explosion of terrible clones and vibe coded mash-ups this month. You can largely thank Anthropic's new 5.5 update to its Claude Opus model for that, which offers massive efficiency gains for vibe coders. It's also been widely used to decompile commercial games and, maybe most famously, jailbreak the PS5.

It definitely feels like we've crossed a threshold this month. On October 10, the creator of Escape the Walls, an incremental punching game which itself uses AI to "increase the speed of creating the game", posted in-progress footage from the game on X.
Prophetically, a user replied: "You have exactly 7 hours before someone makes this on Roblox and gets 20x your revenue".

Right now, on October 19, there are at least seven Roblox clones of Escape the Walls. A competing studio had the audacity to tweet their own clone to the original game's creator. "Our Steam page is live too!" they posted. "Nothing wrong with friendly competition!"

Leaving aside the fact that Escape the Walls is itself pretty crappy looking, the situation highlights the perils of marketing independent games in an age where a clone can be turned around in hours. To wit: as Rick Lane has already reported, the creators of Drunken Goddess Reflux, a "Russian roulette drinking survival" game, has announced it will no longer publish its demo on Steam as planned.
From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

"We are concerned that, based on the content of the demo, works imitating or replicating this game's presentation and gameplay could be quickly produced using AI or other tools and released ahead of the game's launch," a spokesperson for studio Alliance Arts Inc. wrote. The studio will instead hold closed environment play sessions for people who read and agree to a series of "participation requirements".

Elsewhere NoGlyph, the creator of Needle In A Haystack, which is itself a rapid clone of Needle In A Haystack Simulator (see: haystack slop), has accused yet another studio of copying their code in their own clone. "Yesterday, on October 16 a game called A Game About Needle In A Haystack by Little Field Studios came out on Steam," NoGlyph wrote. "It contains code copied from our game. To be clear, this is about our actual code, not a similar idea or similar mechanics."

NoGlyph moves on to offer further proof that the offending studio pulled code directly from their game. "The haystack in our game, meaning how it's drawn, how you dig into it and how gold, lapis and diamond hay work, is something that took a long time to get working properly. When we looked through their game's files, we found 13 of our classes inside it with the exact same names. More than half of the functions in that part match ours exactly. Some of our own error messages are still in there word for word, including one that points to a shader from our project that doesn't exist in their game."
NoGlyph has filed a copyright notice with Valve.

Damn, it sure would be a shame if independent studios stopped releasing demos, or were prevented from marketing their games, because talentless bottom feeders were quickly flipping their ideas into monetizable slop!

Many have made the argument that AI is "good" because it democratises specialised skills and art forms like music, writing, coding, art, and videogame development (which deploys all of the aforementioned). But where videogames are concerned it hasn't democratised anything: it has just emboldened hacks, philistines and scam merchants. Vibe coding a 20 minute blockbuster-looking videogame that resembles the Marvel / Star Wars / Fortnite universes, or vibe coding a Roblox clone of a viral indie, doesn't make you a videogame developer: if anything, it demonstrates why you aren't.

Forgive me, but I don't think someone who hasn't committed time and thought to mastering those pursuits has much hope in producing something valuable with the assistance of AI. You may be able to make something that looks like something else, but you probably don't have ideas. Spending years and years thinking about your craft, being a practitioner, is what generates ideas. Without ideas, you are just playing with the most expensive toy ever built.

Anyone who has made that moronic "democratising" claim has only to look at Roblox and the great piles of worthless slop on Steam to see the actual reality. Steam's discoverability algorithm will probably keep the vast majority of the 8,000+ Next Fest demos out of the public eye, but for those that do go viral, or find an enthusiastic audience, there are hordes of leeches ready to rob you blind, utilising the same technology that's turning PC gaming into a rich person's hobby.
Top Steam games by revenue (October 6 - 13)
You know it's a very boring week on Steam when Dota 2 takes first spot in the revenue chart. So nothing very interesting released, then?
Well, Star Wars: Galactic Racer did, right on October 6, and came in at number four. Given how positive reviews were, and that it's Star Wars, I did kinda expect it to come in at number one.

Gears of War managed to latch onto a top ten position after ranking sixth last week during its first week on sale (it was available as a pre-order before that). Risk of Rain 2 got an actually-decent update and expansion, hence its appearance, and Steam Deck reanimates at number six: there must have been a stock replenishment.
As for Aion 2, people continue to not really like it, based on Steam user reviews, but it's still making bank for NC anyway.
Last week's Steam deep cuts
Last Round at the End of the World | October 13

This fascinating "folk-horror" narrative adventure has an amusing and unsettling art style. Character models are scrapbook collages, and to make things even more uncanny, they're sprite-based. You'll interact with a lot of these weirdos as you navigate, in first-person, the creepy small town of St Nineveh to figure out who deserves sacrificing.
The Doll Shop | October 12

In narrative adventure The Doll Shop you take on the role of small town dollmaker. Holed up in a secluded Japanese village, you live a mostly hermetic existence until a childhood friend rocks up at your door. It looks quaint, but The Doll Shop is described as "part romance, part horror" by its developer, so it's far from a regular cosy experience.
Penguin Colony | October 17

From the creators of Umurangi Generation comes this penguin-centric cosmic horror. Set in Antarctica, you play as a regular ol' penguin forced to witness two human factions prod at a dormant, "ancient and inconceivable" being. It's openly Lovecraft inspired, but the setting and presentation is definitely Origame Digital's own.
Tenebris Somnia | October 17

This stylish survival horror blends FMV with chunky 16-bit pixel art, which somehow makes it feel more disturbingly archaic than if it was one or the other. The Steam page is light on story info, but that's probably for the best. Expect puzzles, prickly encounters, and excessive gore.

Shaun Prescott is the Australian editor of PC Gamer. With over ten years experience covering the games industry, his work has appeared on GamesRadar+, TechRadar, The Guardian, PLAY Magazine, the Sydney Morning Herald, and more. Specific interests include indie games, obscure Metroidvanias, speedrunning, experimental games and FPSs. He thinks Lulu by Metallica and Lou Reed is an all-time classic that will receive its due critical reappraisal one day.

articles.headline: The Simpsons’ Apu Has Finally Spoken on the Show for the First Time in Almost a Decade
keyFacts: The Simpsons character Apu Nahasapeemapetilon spoke for the first time in nearly a decade, voiced by Sunil Malhotra in season 38.
Hank Azaria previously voiced Apu but stepped down in 2020 following criticism of the character's negative portrayal of South Asians.
Executive producer Matt Selman stated that producers wanted to bring the character back in a smart way that allowed him to evolve.
body: After some nine years of being seen but not heard on The Simpsons, the show's creators have finally given a voice back to beloved Kwik-E-Mart owner, Apu Nahasapeemapetilon. In episode three of the series' 38th season dubbed "The Revengening", which aired Sunday night on Fox in the US, a new voice for the loveable Squishee salesman was debuted courtesy of actor and voice-over veteran, Sunil Malhotra (Grey's Anatomy, The Legend of Korra).

According to a report on Variety , Malhotra's hiring and the return of the Apu character – who hasn't uttered a single word on the show since the October 2017 episode, "The Serfsons" – have been heavily kept under wraps, with producers keeping both the episode's table read and its subsequent production under strict NDA for everyone involved.

"We love this character, and wanted to bring him back in a smart, Simpsons-y way that allowed him to evolve," executive producer Matt Selman told Variety. "We're excited by what Sunil has already brought to the role, and look forward to seeing more of Apu in the future."

Hank Azaria previously voiced Apu for the first 29 seasons of the animated series. However, after the character became the focus of the 2017 documentary "The Problem With Apu", in which comedian Hari Kondabolu discussed the negative impact the character has had on people of South Asian descent, Azaria announced that he would no longer lend his voice to the role . Later, during an episode of Dax Shepard's Armchair Expert in 2021, Azaria reflected with remorse about his portrayal of the character and stated that part of him "feels like I need to go to every single Indian person in this country and personally apologise."

After Azaria vacated the role, Apu was pushed to the background on The Simpsons, occasionally seen but never heard. However, after an idea to bring the character back for one of season 38's Halloween-themed episodes was hatched by staffer Nick Hahan and co-executive producer Cesar Mazariegos, the process of finding a new actor for Apu began in earnest.

“When my agent called me about a ‘Simpsons’ audition, I knew exactly what role it was for, and the idea actually made my stomach sink,” Malhotra told Variety. “But admittedly, part of me was also curious. It had been eight years since Apu had spoken on the show, and it got me thinking: Did the writers’ room look different now? Could they bring him back in a way that acknowledged and apologized for past mistakes? Could I make the character my own, and reclaim him in some way? And could they achieve all of that in an unmistakably ‘Simpsons’ way that didn’t disappoint fans?"
After some back and forth with the show's producers, Malhotra was eventually convinced that the return of Apu was being handled in the best possible way.

"It was the beginning of a deeply collaborative experience that I hope is equally satisfying for longtime fans of ‘The Simpsons’ and for other South Asian kids who, like me, stopped watching at some point along the way," said Malhotra.

In "The Revengening", a man in a Daft Punk-inspired Halloween costume is accidentally killed over and over again by residents of Springfield. A year later, the man is still alive and taking his revenge on his would-be killers, one at a time. Eventually the costumed killer is unmasked and revealed to be Apu, who tells the town's residents, "I am the man you left for dead. I am the one you pretended never existed!"

To which Marge, seemingly serving as a mouthpiece for the show's producers, replies, "Apu, we're so sorry we left you for dead. Believe me, wanted to do the right thing." Bart then adds, "But we were so scared, and just didn't know what to do."
For his part, Malhotra seems satisfied with Apu's reintroduction to the cast.

“I’d be lying if I didn’t say that the sweetest part of all was unleashing that righteously rage-fueled “I AM APU!” — on behalf of so many of us — over and over in the studio until we got it just right,” said Malhotra. “I really feel like we did and I can’t wait for fans to see more Apu.”
Have you watched "The Revengening"? What do you think of Sunil Malhotra's portrayal of Apu? Is it a thank you, come again? Let us know in the comments!

articles.headline: Massachusetts GOP ticket rocked by alleged drunken crash as candidate abruptly halts campaign
keyFacts: Shawn Oliver suspended his lieutenant governor campaign after police arrested him for operating under the influence following a rollover crash in New Bedford.
Republican gubernatorial nominee Mike Minogue and New Bedford Mayor Jon Mitchell both called on Oliver to step aside following the crash.
The Department of Correction placed Oliver on restricted work duty at the Massachusetts Treatment Center while the incident is reviewed.
body: A late-night crash has thrown a Massachusetts Republican’s statewide campaign into turmoil just weeks before voters head to the polls.

Shawn Oliver, 42, the Republican nominee for lieutenant governor and a New Bedford city councilor, suspended his campaign on Sunday. The move came after Oliver was arrested following a rollover crash that involved five parked vehicles, police confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Officers responded around 11:40 p.m. Saturday to 448 Dartmouth St., where a vehicle had overturned after striking multiple parked vehicles, the New Bedford Police Department said. Two of the five parked vehicles sustained extensive damage.
BODYCAM SHOWS NANTUCKET OFFICIAL SLURRING, SWAYING DURING DUI STOP AFTER CRASHING INTO SIGN: POLICE
Oliver, identified by police as the driver, was taken to St. Luke’s Hospital for treatment of his injuries.

Following an investigation at the scene and at the hospital, officers arrested Oliver and charged him with operating under the influence of liquor, negligent operation of a motor vehicle, a marked lanes violation and speeding, police said.
DEMOCRAT CANDIDATE SEEN SOBBING, PRAYING IN PATROL CAR AFTER DUI ARREST: VIDEO
Republican gubernatorial nominee Mike Minogue publicly called on Oliver to suspend his campaign.
"I am extremely disappointed. Shawn is lucky to be alive and lucky that no one innocent was hurt," Minogue wrote on X. "There is no excuse for driving under the influence."
NEW JERSEY LT GOV DALE CALDWELL RESIGNS AFTER SEXUAL HARASSMENT INVESTIGATION
Minogue, a businessman and military veteran challenging Democratic Gov. Maura Healey, said he spoke with Oliver before demanding he step aside.
"After speaking with Shawn, I am asking him to suspend his campaign immediately, and when elected, I will formally ask for his resignation," he wrote.
TRAFFIC DRAMA THREATENS TO END DEM GOVERNOR'S TENURE AS VOTERS HEAD TO POLLS IN RHODE ISLAND
Oliver confirmed his campaign suspension on X, saying "the election is too important to be overshadowed by personal matters."
New Bedford Mayor Jon Mitchell said in a statement posted to Facebook that the crash happened in the city’s South End.
MASSACHUSETTS MAYOR CHARGED WITH WIRE FRAUD IN $1.5M COVID RELIEF SCHEME

"This morning, I was made aware that City Councilor Shawn Oliver was involved in a car accident in the South End and taken into custody," Mitchell said. "I’m grateful to the New Bedford Police Department for their prompt response and relieved that no one was seriously injured."
The Democratic mayor also called for Oliver to address the incident publicly.
EX-NEW JERSEY MAYOR, HER HUSBAND CHARGED FOR USING FAKE BALLOT SIGNATURES AFTER SHE PLEADED GUILTY TO DUI
"The allegations against Councilor Oliver are deeply concerning, and the public deserves to hear his explanation of what happened," Mitchell said.
Minogue urged Oliver to focus on his family and take steps to prevent another incident.
"Shawn is a father and grandfather, and he needs to put his family first. He needs to do the work to ensure this never happens again," Minogue wrote. "If he needs help with that, I will help him."
He also took aim at his Democratic opponent.
ICE BOSTON ARRESTS BRAZILIAN ILLEGAL ALIEN WANTED FOR MURDER DAYS BEFORE GOV HEALY SIGNED PROTECT ACT
"As governor, I will put the Commonwealth first. That starts with accountability, something Massachusetts has not seen from Maura Healey," Minogue wrote.

The Massachusetts Department of Correction confirmed to Fox News Digital that Oliver, a New Bedford city councilor employed by the department, has been placed on restricted work duty following his arrest.

"Shawn Oliver has been placed on restricted work duty while all facts and circumstances are reviewed. He is currently assigned to the Massachusetts Treatment Center," department spokesman Scott J. Croteau said.
The campaign suspension comes just weeks before the November election, with Minogue challenging Healey and Democratic Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll seeking another term.

articles.headline: Chamber of Commerce endorses Paxton as he and Talarico host rallies ahead of Texas early voting
keyFacts: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce endorsed Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton on Sunday ahead of early voting.
Paxton and his Democratic opponent, James Talarico, held opposing campaign rallies on Sunday evening to make their closing arguments.
Paxton will host an early voting kickoff event with Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. on Monday night.
body: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce endorsed Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton as he and his opponent, James Talarico , hosted dueling campaign rallies Sunday evening ahead of Texas early voting beginning on Monday.

Talarico hosted a rally in Plano as part of a “major campaign push focused on North Texas,” according to Fox 4 News Dallas-Fort Worth , while Paxton brought his “Come and Take It Tour” to San Antonio. The pair outlined closing arguments for Texas voters as the state’s early voting process begins on Monday .

Paxton has struggled to establish a lead over his Democratic opponent despite Texas’s history as a Republican stronghold and his endorsement from President Donald Trump. Trump’s decision to endorse Paxton over Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX) in the primary election angered some Republicans who believed Cornyn was more likely to win the general election.

“The choice is clear in Texas,” Neil Bradley, Executive Vice President and Chief Policy Officer of the Chamber of Commerce, which is the nation’s largest pro-business group, said on Sunday . “Attorney General Ken Paxton has been a defender of free enterprise and pro-growth policies that empower American businesses to thrive. He has pushed back against federal overreach, helped preserve a low-tax environment, and defended the energy sector from burdensome mandates. Paxton understands that true economic prosperity relies on a fair and predictable justice system. We look forward to working together on meaningful legal reform that shields job creators from lawsuit abuse and red tape.”
TALARICO’S TEXAS-SIZED OPENING: PAXTON CAN’T UNITE REPUBLICAN VOTE

The RealClearPolitics polling average shows Talarico with a slight lead over Paxton. Talarico has largely framed the scandal-plagued Republican candidate as someone unwilling to stand up to Trump’s unpopular policies, while Paxton has hit his Democratic counterpart for previous statements many argue are out of touch with modern Texas voters.

The trade group’s endorsement is unlikely to affect the race and is broadly unsurprising, given that its pro-growth policy stances are largely shared by Republican lawmakers, but it may still bolster a candidate who has otherwise struggled to rally Republican enthusiasm throughout the campaign. Paxton said Sunday he will “get bureaucrats out of the way of the men and women who drive our economy” and said, “If we lost Texas, we lose America.” He will host an early voting kickoff event alongside Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. on Monday night.

articles.headline: Ben Simmons’ NBA comeback derailed after tearing achilles tendon in practice
keyFacts: Sacramento Kings player Ben Simmons tore his right achilles tendon during a practice drill days before the team's season opener.
Simmons will undergo surgery and miss the entire NBA season, pausing his comeback attempt after signing a one-year deal with the Kings.
Simmons stated on Instagram that he will find a way through this latest physical challenge and adversity.
body: Ben Simmons faces a monumental task to revive his NBA career after another devastating injury setback put his comeback attempt with the Sacramento Kings on hold. The Australian will undergo surgery after scans revealed he tore his right achilles tendon during a live drill at practice, just three days out from Sacramento’s season opener against the Los Angeles Clippers.

The 30-year-old signed a one-year deal with the Kings in an attempt to revive his career, but will now miss the entire season. It is another massive setback for the three-time All-Star, after five years battling a series of significant injuries and mental health concerns.

“I’ve faced challenges before that tested me mentally, physically, and emotionally, and I’ve found a way through every single one of them,” Simmons posted in an Instagram story. “This injury is another chapter in my journey, not the end of my story.

“It’s never easy being away from the game I love, especially after everything it took to get back here. But if there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s that adversity doesn’t define you. How you respond to it does. I’ve been knocked down before, and I’ve always found a way to get back up. This time will be no different.”

Simmons had shown promising flashes in pre-season, including a productive 26 minutes in Sacramento’s loss to San Antonio. The build-up had led to high praise from a host of NBA greats, including eight-time All-Star Dwight Howard, who predicted a successful return for the Melbourne-born talent. “Ben Simmons going to have the greatest comeback story in NBA history!” Howard posted on X last week.

NBA legends Dirk Nowitzki and Blake Griffin also recently backed three-time All-Star Simmons to reproduce some of his best basketball this season. “He is incredibly talented, he’s a big body and he can defend so many positions,” Griffin said at the NBA on Prime launch in New York. “Downhill he gets to the rim and he’s a great passer. I want to see a great year from him because he’s a special talent and I think the league is better off with a guy like him in it.”

The latest injury setback continues a rough few years for the former No 1 draft pick, who was named Rookie of the Year and a three-time All-Star before his career went off the rails. Simmons shot to prominence with the Philadelphia 76ers but sat out the 2021-22 season while dealing with mental health concerns and physical injuries. He sought a trade and landed in Brooklyn, where he spent two-and-a-half injury-riddled seasons, and finished the 2024-25 season with the Los Angeles Clippers.

Simmons was cut at the end of that campaign and sat out all of last season, leading critics to question whether he had lost his love for basketball. He rubbished those claims after inking his return with Sacramento and was set to play a key role for the rebuilding Kings alongside rookie Darius Acuff and fellow veteran Zach LaVine.

articles.headline: Linux KVM guest-host escape rated critical, may represent a new way to attack penguin-powered networking
keyFacts: Researcher Paulos Yibelo identified a critical Linux KVM guest-host escape flaw designated CVE-2026-99999 and named PwnEscape.
Red Hat reported that malformed IPv4 packets can corrupt network headers, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution, system crashes, or information disclosure on the host.
Developers have created an upstream fix in the Linux kernel that is being distributed to major Linux distributions and virtualization products.
body: Paulos Yibelo, the researcher who in early October claimed to have found a guest-host escape flaw in Linux KVM, the hypervisor used by most hyperscale clouds, has named the flaw PwnEscape and warned it might represent a new way to attack Linux – on top of being a 9.3-rated critical nasty in its own right. Yibelo’s work is now CVE-2026-99999. It is a scary bug because it makes a guest-host escape possible with a few malformed IPv4 packets. Such attacks are a nightmare security scenario because the whole point of virtualization is carving up hardware into isolated “guest” virtual machines that share a “host” server’s resources – without ever being able to see what other guests or the host are doing. Public clouds rely on that isolation remaining impervious. So do private clouds, because if guest/host isolation is violated, an attacker could conceivably access all the VMs on a host or pool of virtualized hardware. Attacks on a host could give an evildoer access to thousands of VMs, plus containers because many developers now run those constructs in a micro-VM to keep them isolated. PwnEscape makes it possible for guests to access the host, by sending a guest malformed IPv4 packets. As explained in a message from Red Hatter Michael S. Tsirkin in the Linux kernel stable tree, ‘If a packet with bad checksum metadata gets into the ipv4 stack, skb_checksum_help can corrupt the network header and cause a bunch of mischief.” Analysis from threat-finding firm SOC Prime details the mischief. “Linux allows network packets to carry metadata indicating where a checksum operation should begin and where its result should be written. This optimization is legitimate and widely used for checksum offloading, but the security problem arises when less-trusted guest-controlled metadata can influence a write after the packet header has already passed earlier validation stages.” “Because the disclosure could be triggered repeatedly, an attacker controlling a guest workload could potentially collect information from a security domain that the virtual machine should not be able to inspect. This represents a direct failure of the guest-host isolation boundary.” Red Hat’s report says the impact can potentially include “arbitrary code execution on the host, a system crash resulting in Denial of Service, or information disclosure of sensitive memory.” A new class of threat Paulos Yibelo, the researcher who found the flaw, thinks he stumbled upon a novel attack. “As far as we know, PwnEscape exposes an entirely new class of attacks in Linux networking: untrusted checksum metadata can rewrite security-sensitive packet fields after the kernel has already validated and acted on them, undermining assumptions across the networking stack far beyond the original VM escape,” he wrote. “The popular mental model is that VM isolation lives in the virtual-machine monitor. Much of it does. But an attacker-controlled workload does not interact only with arch/x86/kvm/. It interacts with a host OS full of optimized, highly composable interfaces.” “If the metadata crosses a trust boundary, every deferred consumer has to inherit the right invariants. And if the packet can be transformed after those invariants are checked, the invariants have to remain true in the new representation.” “That is why a bug that looks, at first, like a malformed checksum hint can become a memory disclosure and a guest-to-host escape primitive. The problem was not how difficult IPv4 is to parse. It was that different parts of Linux were allowed to trust different versions of the same packet.” That’s an important observation, because while Linux KVM is widely used, and free, it is part of Linux – a project comprised of over 40 million lines of code. A vendor named Edera, which offers a secure container runtime based on the Xen hypervisor, last week none-too-gently pointed out that’s a big attack surface and that researchers have found seven escape bugs this year alone including Januscape. AWS, which runs its cloud on KVM, says its elastic compute cloud is not at risk. Google Cloud’s method of using KVM means it is probably in the clear, too. Developers have created an upstream fix in the Linux kernel. It’s percolating into major distros like Debian, RHEL, and Ubuntu and hopefully into virtualization products that rely on KVM, such as Nutanix and Proxmox. In the age of AI, miscreants will doubtless quickly explore Yibelo’s discoveries, making PwnScape potentially quite a moment for Linux developers and users. ®

articles.headline: What do all the lights on your Netgear router mean, and which ones actually matter?
keyFacts: Netgear routers feature various lights and symbols on the front that indicate power, internet connection status, and Wi-Fi activity.
Understanding the different colors and blinking patterns of these router indicators is important for troubleshooting network issues.
Mesh systems like the Netgear Orbi use minimalist front and back lights to represent connection quality and power status.
body: What do all the lights on your Netgear router mean, and which ones actually matter?
Depending on their colors, most of those flashing lights are a good sign.

The front of a Netgear router, like many routers, is dotted with a wide array of lights and symbols. Though some of the symbols like the power indicator are straightforward, the lights themselves can be much less clear. They often vary in color; sometimes they're blinking and other times they're solid. If you've never picked up the manual, deciphering what each of the many lights means doesn't come naturally.

Understanding what each of the indicators on your Netgear router signify is important for troubleshooting, as well as making sure everything is running as it should. Although some lights are usually more important than others, they all serve a purpose. Whether you have a standard router or one of the company's mesh Wi-Fi systems, this is how to better understand what your Netgear device is telling you.
The most important lights on your Netgear router
These are the lights on a router that are generally the most important to pay attention to, as they're indicators of the most impactful stats like power and overall internet connection status.
The power LED
Represented by the typical power symbol, this indicates information about your device's firmware, as well as its power status. Unsurprisingly, this will be off if your router has no power.
- Solid green or white: The router is on and ready.
- Solid amber: The router is turning on.
- Blinking amber: The router's firmware is upgrading, or you pressed the reset button.
- Blinking white: The router's firmware is corrupted.

- Blinking white and amber: The router is in access point mode, which means it's acting as a connection point for other devices instead of handling its normal router functions. Some features like VPN and remote management will be unavailable.
If your router isn't working properly, restart it first. In case it's fully unresponsive, you may need to do a factory reset.
Internet LED
The icon and light with a small circle orbiting a larger one shows your general connection status:
- Off: The router is not connected to a modem; check the Ethernet cable to make sure it's fully inserted and not damaged.
- Solid green or white: The internet connection is ready.
- Solid amber: An Ethernet cable connection to the modem has been detected.
- Blinking white: The port is sending and/or receiving traffic.
Wi-Fi LED
Represented by a small dot with two curves on each side, this light shows general Wi-Fi traffic.
- Off: The router's Wi-Fi radios are off.
- Solid white: The router's Wi-Fi radios are operating.
- Blinking white: The router is sending and/or receiving Wi-Fi traffic.
Other lights on your Netgear router
Further lights on your Netgear router are more useful for specific troubleshooting, or if you're plugging additional devices into the router.
Wi-Fi band LEDS

Every modern router should have lights for the 2.4GHz and 5GHz bands, as these have long been the standard. For a Wi-Fi 6E model or newer, you'll also see a 6GHz light for that modern band. The lights will differ depending on the bands currently in use, but the lights have the same meanings for each band.
- Off: This particular Wi-Fi radio is off.
- Solid white: The Wi-Fi radio in question is operating.
- Blinking white: The router is sending and/or receiving traffic over the corresponding Wi-Fi radio.
USB LEDs
Your router will have one of these lights for each USB port it includes, represented by the trident USB symbol or the text "USB 3.0."
- Off: No USB device is connected to the port, or the Safely Remove Hardware button was pressed and you're clear to remove the attached device.
- Blinking: A USB device is trying to connect.
- Solid green or white: A USB device is connected and ready to use.
Ethernet LEDs

These are labeled by numbers, with each representing an Ethernet port on the router. The color represents the speed of the connection: white or green for 1 Gbps connections, and amber for slower 100 Mbps or 10 Mbps Ethernet.
- Off: Nothing is connected to the port.
- Solid: A powered-on device is connected to the port.
- Blinking: The port is sending and/or receiving traffic.
WPS LED

Represented by what looks like a router with signals coming out of it, this light indicates the success of a WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup) connection, which allows you to add devices to your network without entering the network name and password. For the best router security, you should disable this.
- Off: No WPS connection.
- Blinking: A WPS connection is in progress.
- Solid: The WPS connection was successful.
Reading the lights on a Netgear Orbi mesh system

The lights on Netgear's Orbi Wi-Fi mesh system are minimalist compared to a typical router's, and represent key statuses slightly differently. There's a light in the bottom-front of the device, plus one at the back. The light in the front represents the connection status, while the one at the back is tied to the device's power and firmware.
The front LED lights
- Solid blue light: The connection between the router and satellite is strong.
- Solid amber light: The connection between the router and satellite is OK, but not great.
- Solid magenta light: There's no backhaul connection or no internet connection.
- No light: The Orbi is not receiving power.
The back LED light
- Solid green light: The router and satellite are powered on.
- Solid amber light: The device is rebooting.
- Pulsing amber light: The device is updating its firmware or resetting to factory settings.
- Pulsing red light: Possible hardware issues or connectivity failure.
- No light: The Orbi is not receiving power.

articles.headline: Arm AGI CPU crushes AMD in new agentic AI benchmark — but what does its 2x rack-level performance advantage mean for the future of x86 data centers?
keyFacts: An assessment by Signal65 with Arm's cooperation found that Arm's AGI CPU achieved nearly twice the modelled rack-level performance of AMD's EPYC 9755 across seven agentic AI workloads.
The modelled advantage is largely driven by power consumption differences, allowing a 24-kW rack to house more Arm servers than dual-socket AMD systems within the same electricity limit.
Arm executive vice president Mohamed Awad stated that the industry needs to measure how well systems handle the work agents actually complete.
body: - Arm’s AGI CPU nearly doubles AMD’s modelled rack-level performance across seven workloads
- A 24-kW rack accommodates up to 23 Arm servers under the assessment’s assumptions
- Arm’s rack-level advantage reaches 3.19x in the strongest individual workload
Arm’s AGI CPU has recorded nearly twice the modelled rack-level performance of AMD’s EPYC 9755 across seven workloads designed to evaluate agentic artificial intelligence.
The assessment, conducted by Signal65 with Arm’s cooperation, compared measured processor results before estimating performance across racks operating within a fixed power budget.
The findings rely partly on power-based modelling, while testing on final production hardware remains outstanding.
Rack density gives Arm a substantial advantage
The assessment examined workloads involving software tools, autonomous task execution, information retrieval, and support for AI model serving, including Terminal-Bench 2 and SWE-bench.
Across the seven tests, Arm’s processor achieved an average performance ratio of 1.99x, with individual results ranging from 1.43x to 3.19x compared with AMD’s EPYC 9755.
The modelled advantage partly comes from differences in server power consumption, allowing more Arm systems within the same electricity allocation.
A 24 kW rack could accommodate 21 to 23 AGI CPU servers, compared with 13 dual-socket EPYC 9755 systems.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
That configuration provides between 5,712 and 5,888 physical cores for Arm, compared with 3,328 for AMD, although the comparison depends on the rated power assumptions.
Individual server power ranges from 950 to 1,050 watts for Arm’s systems, while AMD’s dual-socket configurations carry a rated consumption of 1,700 watts.
Across workload categories, Arm recorded modelled rack-level advantages averaging 1.7x for tooling, 2.0x for agentic workflows and 2.2x for reasoning and planning.
The report also estimated that database and vector-search operations could require 30% to 35% fewer racks for equivalent processing workloads.
Faster sandbox creation and the x86 challenge
Separate testing compared Arm’s processor against AMD’s EPYC 9965 using Sandbench, which measures the time required to establish isolated execution environments.
Arm completed cold starts 45% faster, warm starts 27% faster, and its worst-case scenario under fourfold oversubscription 41% faster.
These improvements matter because AI agents frequently create execution environments while accessing services, running code, and processing information.
Faster setup can reduce delays, although the results do not demonstrate equivalent gains across all applications or complete data center deployments.

Arm executive vice president for Cloud AI Mohamed Awad said, “The industry needs to measure how well systems handle the work agents actually complete,” describing the need for workload-specific performance evaluation.
The company developed its evaluation framework with support from Fujitsu, Meta and OpenAI, while Signal65 independently verified the reported processor results.
Arm also acknowledged that further testing on final production systems would cover additional workloads and competitive comparisons.
For AMD and Intel, the findings suggest that Arm-based servers could challenge x86 infrastructure in agentic AI deployments where rack power limits constrain computing capacity.
Higher rack-level performance could let operators accommodate more AI workloads within existing power allocations.
However, the benchmark does not establish that Arm will outperform x86 across general-purpose computing or justify replacing existing servers across entire data centers.
Software compatibility, deployment costs and real-world operating conditions will influence whether the modelled advantage translates into wider adoption.

articles.headline: Outrage after Meta suspends No Kings Instagram account during protests
keyFacts: Meta temporarily suspended the No Kings protest movement's Instagram account during nationwide demonstrations, later apologizing and calling it an automated error.
Organizers and lawmakers condemned the suspension, with Senator Chris Murphy calling for an investigation into Meta's political influence.
Organizers said they planned to recruit volunteers during the events to mobilize against potential election sabotage.
body: The coalition leaders behind nationwide pro-democracy protests that have drawn millions of Americans to the streets in recent years were frustrated when its Instagram account was temporarily shut down during its latest demonstration on Saturday.
The No Kings movement’s account went dark for several hours while protests focused on increasing early voter turnout were underway, sparking censorship fears.
Meta apologized on Saturday and blamed the account’s temporary suspension on an automated action that’s triggered “when accounts post, share or comment at very high frequencies”.
“Unfortunately, that automated action was clearly taken in error,” Meta spokesperson Andy Stone, wrote on X. “Everything is now working as it should and we sincerely apologize.”

“We have regained access to our accounts, but Meta still owes us an explanation,” the No Kings Coalition posted on their Instagram page, on Sunday. “Restricting communications about voting in the middle of an election is unacceptable.”
In a longer statement, Stone cited the “high volume” of reading profiles, posts and hashtags in “intense bursts” on Saturday caused their AI tool to detect the activity as automated bot traffic.

“This activity caused our automated protections to incorrectly take the No Kings Instagram account offline. An automated re-review of the removal action an hour later recognized that shouldn’t have happened and restored the account,” Stone said. “It unfortunately took additional time for us to straighten out the situation with admin access to the IG account. We want to reiterate our sincere apology for the error.”
Organizers remained skeptical about Meta’s explanation that high-frequency posting triggered an automated response, and said members “posted only a handful of times and livestreamed to thousands”.
Senator Bernie Sanders also expressed concerns on Sunday, on X, saying that “billionaire ownership of the media” had resulted in the suspension of the No Kings account.

Connecticut senator Chris Murphy called for an investigation into the incident in his own social media post, saying it was an indictment of Meta’s “outsized influence” on US culture and politics. “How were they not ready for the biggest day of anti-Trump protest of the campaign?” Murphy said. “An investigation is warranted, at the very least, to understand why Meta (which effectively functions these days as a private government) was unable to protect protest against Trump, while it spends so much time trying to get close to Trump.”

Despite the technical blip, hundreds of planned events continued. At the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, a band played for a few hundred people in caps and coats, many of whom were dancing and held signs saying “VOTE EARLY” and “HANDS OFF MY VOTE!”
In Atlanta, city councilman Michael Julian Bond told the crowd: “The constitution gives you one power, right? That is the power to vote. Are you gonna use that power?”

On the streets of downtown Los Angeles, protesters carried umbrellas to protect them from the sweltering heat and a band trailed behind them on a rolling stage, the New York Times reported; the crowds cheered calls for abolishing ICE and passing California’s billionaire tax.

The No Kings movement began last summer, in response to a broad set of concerns about federal layoffs, immigration enforcement and foreign wars. The demonstrations have continued to tackle a wide range of issues, and typically lean into anti-Trump fervor.

This year’s focus on voting ahead of the midterm elections is in part due to the supreme court’s gutting of the Voting Rights Act, as well as fears about Trump once again sowing chaos by baselessly calling election results into question.

No Kings organizers said they planned to recruit volunteers at Saturday’s events to mobilize in case of “election sabotage”, Leah Greenberg, a co-executive director of Indivisible, a progressive group that helps organize No Kings events, previously told the Guardian.

articles.headline: MrBeast Joins Shark Tank, Invests Quarter Million In AI-Powered ‘Ball 2’
keyFacts: YouTube creator James Stephen Donaldson, known as MrBeast, debuted as an investor on Shark Tank and invested $250,000 for a 55% stake in Ball 2.
Cousins Andrew Brown and Kevin Langdon presented Ball 2, an AI-powered ball filled with sensors that tracks data and connects to a companion app to create new games.
While other investors expressed skepticism regarding consumer interest and marketing, Donaldson and the creators expressed confidence in generating viral appeal.
body: James Stephen Donaldson, the algorithm ruling, product hustling, normal smile having YouTube superstar better known as MrBeast recently made his debut on Shark Tank. During his first episode on the show where celebrity investors put “idea people” through a humiliation ritual, Donaldson cut from the pack to back an AI-powered ball. It rolls. You can throw it. Itâs, yâknow, got AI in there. Donaldson opted to invest a quarter million into the product.

Cousins Andrew Brown and Kevin Langdon presented the Sharks with “Ball 2.” A sequel to ball. Unlike your average foam ball, the second ball is “filled with sensors,” capable of tracking and harvesting data as it is rolled, thrown, bounced and so forth. Reporting information back to a companion app, Brown and Langdon added that through the magic of AI you can instruct the ball to create new games on the fly. Like being thrown further, or being rolled not as far.

For a live demonstration, Donaldson and Lori Greiner competed to see who could shake the ball more. Donaldson won. “It worked way better than I was expecting it to work,” said Donaldson after getting his shake on, “that was cool.”

For the most part, the Sharks seemed characteristically unimpressed by Ball 2. Their primary concern was marketing to consumers. The world is full of balls. There are millions of ball havers. Thousands of ball knowers. And despite disagreements from certain communities, we even live on a giant ball. All balls without AI, and at first glance the ball with AI in it looks no different. Without coming across the video pitch, there would be little motivation to opt-in. “If you put this next to another ball on a shelf itâs a tough sell,” admits Langdon.

While Mr. Wonderful withheld his support, MrBeast was all-in. Donaldson invested $250 thousand for a 55% stake in the company. After a concerned glance at each other, the two cousins turned around and shouted “beast ball!” to the offer. Greiner and O’Leary were skeptical of consumer interest, the latter saying it would live or die on a “viral” moment. Donaldson lives and dies on that same principle, fashioning himself a scholar of YouTube user trends and unironic appreciator of Squid Game (the show and the practice). With a seemingly hypnotic control over nephews and their energy drink consumption, both Donaldson and the Ball 2 crew seemed confident they could get kids interested in their AI play orb.

At just 28 years-old, Donaldson has established a business empire that is as vast as it is dubious. While he boasts about his surgical mastery over social media, he plays it far faster and looser in his other ventures. Whether itâs the quality of his food products, routine allegations over staff treatment or where he decides to open a theme park, his circle of control seems to wane the further you go offline.
As for me, I’m keeping my money in Aurora Castle, the amusement park that’s also a space colony to be built somewhere in Vaughan.
